title.en: European Commission proposes the first comprehensive AI regulation framework
title.zhHans: 欧盟委员会提出全球首个综合性 AI 监管框架

searchSummary.en: The EU AI Act proposal (April 2021) — the world’s first comprehensive AI regulation. How Europe proposed a risk-based framework for governing AI that reshaped global tech policy.
searchSummary.zhHans: 欧盟 AI 法案提案（2021 年 4 月）——世界上第一部全面的 AI 监管法规。欧洲提出的基于风险的 AI 治理框架如何重塑了全球科技政策。

summary.en: In April 2021, the European Commission proposed the first comprehensive AI law — the EU AI Act. It introduced a risk-based classification system: AI applications deemed 'unacceptable risk' (like social scoring or real-time biometric surveillance) would be banned, while 'high-risk' systems (like hiring or credit scoring tools) would face strict compliance requirements. The proposal marked the beginning of serious AI governance, creating a regulatory template that would influence laws worldwide. After three years of negotiation and amendment, it was finally approved in March 2024.
summary.zhHans: 2021 年 4 月，欧盟委员会提出了第一部全面的 AI 法律——欧盟 AI 法案。它引入了基于风险的分类体系：被认为"不可接受风险"的 AI 应用（如社会评分或实时生物识别监控）将被禁止，而"高风险"系统（如招聘或信用评分工具）将面临严格的合规要求。该提案标志着严肃 AI 治理的开始，创建了一个影响全球法律的监管模板。经过三年的谈判和修订，它最终于 2024 年 3 月获得批准。

narrative.en: The EU AI Act proposal was the culmination of years of discussion within the European Union about how to regulate emerging technology. The European Commission's approach was distinctive: instead of regulating AI technology directly, it regulated AI applications based on their risk to human rights and safety. The risk categories were: unacceptable risk (banned), high risk (strict compliance obligations), limited risk (transparency requirements), and minimal risk (no obligations). The proposal covered a wide range of AI applications — from chatbots (requiring disclosure that you're talking to AI) to biometric identification (banned in most public contexts). The proposed enforcement mechanism was powerful: fines up to €30 million or 6% of global annual turnover for violations. The proposal triggered intense lobbying from tech companies, debates about regulatory overreach versus necessary safeguards, and a three-year legislative process involving the European Parliament and EU member states. The UK, US, China, and other jurisdictions watched closely — some as models to follow, others as cautionary tales of regulatory burden. The final Act was approved in March 2024, with enforcement phased in through 2025-2027. The April 2021 proposal was the moment AI governance became a real political force.
narrative.zhHans: 欧盟 AI 法案提案是欧盟内部多年来关于如何监管新兴技术讨论的顶点。欧盟委员会的方法独具特色：不是直接监管 AI 技术，而是根据 AI 应用对人权和安全的风险来监管。风险类别为：不可接受风险（禁止）、高风险（严格合规义务）、有限风险（透明度要求）和最低风险（无义务）。该提案涵盖了广泛的 AI 应用——从聊天机器人（要求披露你在与 AI 对话）到生物识别（在大多数公共场合禁止）。拟议的执行机制非常强大：违规罚款最高 3000 万欧元或全球年营业额的 6%。该提案引发了科技公司的大力游说、关于监管过度与必要保障的辩论，以及涉及欧洲议会和欧盟成员国的三年立法过程。英国、美国、中国和其他司法管辖区密切关注——有些作为追随的榜样，有些作为监管负担的警示。最终法案于 2024 年 3 月获批，执行分阶段在 2025-2027 年展开。2021 年 4 月的提案是 AI 治理成为真正政治力量的那一刻。

description.en: First comprehensive AI regulation proposal. Established the risk-based framework that became the global template for AI governance. Triggered three years of legislative negotiation, culminating in the world's first comprehensive AI law in 2024.
description.zhHans: 首个全面 AI 监管提案。建立了成为全球 AI 治理模板的基于风险框架。引发了三年立法谈判，最终在 2024 年形成世界第一部全面 AI 法律。

text.en: The European Commission proposed the first comprehensive EU AI law in April 2021, introducing a risk-based classification system for AI applications.
